Q: What is a 'closure'? A:

Here is another real-life example, and using a scripting language popular in games, Lua. I needed to slightly change the way a library function worked to avoid a problem with standard input not being available.

local old_dofile = dofile

function dofile(filename)
  if filename == nil then
    error('Can not use default of standard input.')
  end

  old_dofile(filename)
end

The value of old_dofile disappears when this block of code finishes its scope (because it's local). However, the value has been enclosed in a closure, so the new redefined dofile function can access it, or rather a copy stored along with the function as an 'upvalue'.

Q: Adding characters at the start and end of each line in a file A:

If you want to wrap text, preserving indentation:

%s/^\s*\zs.*/"&"/g

If you want to do this for a selection, select in visual mode, then the command will be:

'<,'>s/^\s*\zs.*/"&"

Q: Task Scheduler did not launch task "\abc" because instance "(GUID)" of the same task is already running A:

Sorry to come so late to this party, but i ran into this problem today too:

Task Scheduler did not launch task "\task" because instance "{xxxxxxx-adc9-xxxx-8830-a68f5ae629a1}" of the same task is already running.

This message was generated in the History logs of Tasksched and i searched for this exact query on Google and found this thread. I leave my take/approach on this before i forget about it, so i could find it next time if i will ever get into this trouble.

My main bafflement was the fact that i have other tasks that run very well with no problem/trouble of what so ever.

So my approach was to compare all of them to see and try to spot the diffrences between them.

Than, i read what user27489646 had to say and especially the part with:

"In Action tab filled in follwing:

for Program/script: Powershell add arguments (optional):  Powershell-executionpolicy bypass -File E:[path to script]\scriptname.ps1"

This got me a bit thinking.

What i had in the Program/script was powershell.exe

In my add arguments (optional): powershell.exe -windowstyle minimized -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "X:\Folder\Run\wrapper\run_auto.ps1"

What trick did it for me was to change from this:

powershell.exe -windowstyle minimized -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "X:\Folder\Run\wrapper\run_auto.ps1"
To this:
powershell.exe -windowstyle minimized -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File X:\Folder\Run\wrapper\run_auto.ps1

Notice the fact that in the changed form i ditched both of ""

And now works as intended.

Probably if i put just the first " one would work fine also, but i beg the question: But Why?! ^^

Q: Vectorize calculating compound interest with vector of rates and contributions A: 
sum(rev(cumprod(rev(c(RateVector, 0) + 1))) * c(StartingBalance, ContributionVector))

[1] 14151.2

Something's up with the precision here, but it's within a cent of your value. If you want the vector of all values, your current solution will be your best bet. If you tried to apply the above solution to get that vector (e.g., using sapply), it'd be at least O(N^2), whereas I believe your solution is O(N).

To break it down:

rev(cumprod(rev(c(RateVector, 0) + 1))) is a vector of the amount that a contribution at the corresponding time step will grow by the end. We append 0 to the end of the rate vector since the last contribution won't grow at all. We use rev twice so that the cumulative product runs backwards. c(StartingBalance, ContributionVector), then is the contribution at the corresponding time step, treating StartingBalance as the first contribution.
